clue.text: Promotion of friendly relations in House Of Cards?

definitions.meaning: work to foster good relations between rival groups or nations
read literally, construction made of playing cards, as used in the card game of bridge

explanation.surface: A political drama about diplomacy, perhaps the TV series House of Cards.
explanation.walkthrough: House of Cards looks like the TV drama; read literally it is a structure built from playing cards, and bridge is a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomats speak of mending ties between communities as constructing metaphorical spans across a divide.

clue.text: Wide minor thoroughfare picked out by car's spotlight?

parts.note: a B road is a minor British road, below an A road
a headlight's shaft of light is its beam, so something lit up is in it

explanation.surface: A wide little lane is caught in a car's headlights at night.
explanation.walkthrough: A B road is a secondary route in Britain's road numbering.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from ships, meaning broad across the hips or width, so simply wide.

clue.text: Break actually is around end of summer

indicators.note: the phrase for actually is placed around the next letter

parts.note: in fact means actually

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of summer

explanation.surface: Something genuinely breaks as summer draws to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is around' puts R (the end of 'summer') inside IN FACT.
explanation.definitionFit: To infract is to violate or breach a rule, a legal synonym for break.

clue.text: Crazy journey touring round New Zealand

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the journey and round letters surround the country

parts.note: to go is to journey
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A wild trip around New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' signals the country's abbreviation going inside the journey and the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gonzo describes something bizarre or wildly unconventional, as in gonzo journalism, so mad or crazy.

clue.text: Comparatively tired old king transported to grave thus?

indicators.note: thus says the old king lies on the stand, so his name goes inside it

parts.note: a bier is the stand on which a coffin or corpse is carried to the grave
Lear is Shakespeare's ancient British king

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch borne to burial looks more worn out than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thus' points to the king lying on the frame that carries the dead, as Lear is borne off at the end of Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary eyes are dim from fatigue, and the comparative form means more tired.

clue.text: Pictures how pupils are grouped by ability?

definitions.meaning: small illustrations set within a larger picture or page

definitions.text: how pupils are grouped by ability?
definitions.meaning: British schools stream pupils into ability bands called sets

explanation.surface: Visual aids illustrate how a school divides its children by aptitude.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools pupils taught by ability are said to be placed in sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Small images placed within a larger picture or map are known by this term.

clue.text: Almost get rid of crude-sounding speech

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to diss is to dismiss or reject with contempt

indicators.note: sounding says a word with the same sound as the one for crude is used

parts.note: crude means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: A plea to banish nearly all vulgar talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts DISS to DIS; 'sounding' turns COARSE into COURSE, which is said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a formal talk or written treatment of a subject, a kind of speech.

clue.text: Composer set up a German school in London, note

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means written bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: ein is German for a
LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A musician founds a German school in London, it is noted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses EIN to NIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Nielsen was the Danish symphonist, a renowned composer.

clue.text: Do-gooders distributed the grain in British city

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the city

parts.note: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire

indicators.note: distributed means the letters are spread around in a new order

explanation.surface: Charity workers hand out grain in a British city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' makes INGHEART from 'the grain', and 'in' puts that inside the Yorkshire city.
explanation.definitionFit: A disparaging term for people seen as excessively sympathetic liberals, so do-gooders.

clue.text: Wrongdoers finish up hiding among unopened boxes

indicators.note: hiding among puts the word for finish inside the trimmed boxes
unopened means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: coffers are strong boxes
to finish up is to end

explanation.surface: Criminals stash something in unopened crates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' leaves OFFERS from the strong boxes; 'hiding among' puts the finish inside.
explanation.definitionFit: People who commit offences are criminals or wrongdoers.

clue.text: Casserole reduced by a pound: a bargain

indicators.note: reduced means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a stew is a casserole
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A casserole marked down by a pound is good value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts STEW to STE. 'Reduced' looks like cooking or a price cut, but it trims the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bought very cheaply is colloquially called this, a real bargain.

clue.text: Old knave maybe knocked back, seeing stars

indicators.note: knocked back means the letters are turned round

parts.note: a knave is an example of a playing card

explanation.surface: An old rogue, rebuffed, sees stars as if punched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns O + CARD into DRACO.
explanation.definitionFit: Draco is a northern constellation, the Dragon, a group of stars.

clue.text: Tatty trousers 'e turned up

indicators.note: tatty means shabby, so the letters are knocked into a new shape

parts.note: a Cockney he, dropping the h, gives the letter E

explanation.surface: A cockney's scruffy trousers have been hitched up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tatty' rearranges TROUSERS + E.
explanation.definitionFit: A retroussé nose is turned up at the tip, a French borrowing.

clue.text: No bank will accept a single franc, teller revealed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: will accept means the row takes the single and franc inside it

parts.note: a tier is a bank or row, as of seats
I is the Roman numeral for one
F is the abbreviation for franc

explanation.surface: No bank will take a lone franc, a cashier reveals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teller' looks like a bank cashier; here it is someone who tells or informs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives notice of something tells it, so an informant or teller.

clue.text: Stop Nottingham team getting ahead of the entire field?

indicators.note: getting ahead of places the team's name in front of the next word

parts.note: Nottingham Forest is a football club
all means the entire field of competitors

explanation.surface: A football club leads the whole field in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Nottingham Forest is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to prevent or head off something in advance, so stop.

clue.text: Book published that is about part of Borneo

parts.note: a newspaper story that is run is published

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned round

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A published book about a region of a large Asian island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns IE into EI.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small sultanate on the north coast of the island of Borneo.

clue.text: Hold hair to give protection from the sun

parts.note: to have is to hold
a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: Keep your hair on to shield your head from sunburn.
explanation.definitionFit: A havelock is a cloth cover on a cap hanging over the neck, shading it from heat.

clue.text: Man finishes off home brew

indicators.note: finishes off means each word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A man polishes off his homemade beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishes off' looks like drinking up; it removes the final letters of HOME and BREW.
explanation.definitionFit: Hombre is Spanish for man, used in English slang for a guy.

clue.text: Be involved in cunning match play

indicators.note: involved in puts the first word inside the rearranged letters
cunning means crafty, so the letters are artfully rearranged

explanation.surface: Get mixed up in a crafty game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunning' rearranges MATCH to MACTH, and 'involved in' puts BE in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth is Shakespeare's Scottish tragedy, a stage play.

clue.text: Wader got nervous, seeing canine swimming?

indicators.note: nervous means jittery, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A wading bird grew jumpy on spotting a dog in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervous' rearranges WADER GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog bred to retrieve from water, like a water spaniel, is a swimming canine.

clue.text: Rookie in river, grabbing floating platform

indicators.note: grabbing means the river takes hold of the platform inside it

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a raft is a floating platform

explanation.surface: A novice in a river clutches a raft.
explanation.definitionFit: A draftee is a conscript newly called up, so a raw recruit.

clue.text: Drunk became panicky, losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter goes

parts.note: to flap is to get into a panic

explanation.surface: A drunk lost his nerve and then his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like intoxicated; here it is the past tense of drink, as a cat drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap liquid is to drink it with the tongue, so lapped is drunk.

clue.text: Theatre promoter briefly keeps male away from the spotlight

indicators.note: keeps means the shortened word holds the male inside
briefly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a backer funds a theatre production
a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: A theatre investor keeps a man out of the limelight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' leaves BACKE from the promoter; 'keeps' holds the male deer inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind the scenes of a theatre, out of view of the audience, is out of the limelight.

clue.text: College girl turned in several compositions

indicators.note: turned says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A female student appears in several of the pieces she wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters ERALC sitting across the two words; 'turned' reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Clare is a Cambridge college and also a girl's first name.

clue.text: Empty container — fish basket

indicators.note: empty means the inside letters are removed, leaving the first and last

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An empty container is a fishing basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' leaves CR from CONTAINER.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket used by anglers to carry fish.

clue.text: Behind a park there's a nut tree

indicators.note: behind means the park comes after the first article

parts.note: rec is short for recreation ground, a park

explanation.surface: A nut tree grows at the back of a park.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec is British slang for a public recreation ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The areca is a palm tree whose seed is the betel nut.

clue.text: Person paid by examination board? I object

definitions.note: a cry of dissent, standing for one who dissents

parts.note: a pro is a professional, paid for work
a tester is one who sets exams

explanation.surface: A paid examiner raises an objection.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: someone who objects might well cry this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dissents publicly says, in effect, that they object.

clue.text: They risked all, wickedly pinching large picture

indicators.note: pinching means the rearranged letters steal and hold the next letter inside
wickedly means naughtily, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Thieves gambled everything to steal a big painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wickedly' rearranges THEY RISKED ALL and 'pinching' takes L inside. 'Picture' is a film here, a 1955 Ealing comedy about robbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ladykillers is a classic Ealing film, and a picture is a movie.
